post_content:
A "<=" operator cost me 7 test cases today. Those 7 test cases cost me a
possibly good opportunity for me today. Nevertheless, I cannot ignore the fact
that I was COMPLETELY at fault. As soon as I understood the question, I
started coding as if someone had held me at gunpoint. I don't know what had
come into me. I never do this!! I always make the logic on paper and then
code. Now, all I feel is regret and disappointment. But, before I drown in the
pool of thoughts that will just bring me down, two things that I am going to
keep in mind from now on: 1) Do not code before making the logic on paper. 2)
Do not, in any case, forget rule 1. That should do, for anxious people like
me! :) hashtag#mymistakes hashtag#myfailurestory hashtag#missedopportunities

profile_headline: I could give hundred eye catchy titles but I choose to be me!
post_content:
Where did this men shouldn't, can't, don't or won't cry come from? Why was
that practiced? Any genuine reason or is it only because men are from Mars
thing? In late Sri. VGs funeral, I noticed senior minister SMK holding back
his tears badly, so did his own sons. I doubt it's because of camera. I have
seen even my dad struggling to hold back tears till he finally gave up when he
saw his grown up daughters death. I have seen my own brother holding back his
tears till he couldn't hold back anymore when my dad died. I have seen my own
son silently tap footing around death because he doesn't want to cry for his
own granddad who played major role in his upbringing! It's been followed and
practiced since generations!!! Why is it so much of a struggle? Isn't tears
are meant to clean your eyes and clear your mind? If it is, why is it gender
specific? hashtag#genuinequestion hashtag#notfrivolous hashtag#mendontcry
hashtag#life hashtag#lifeslittlelessons.
